momentum.label: Momentum (12-1)
momentum.blurb: The cumulative return over months t-12 to t-2, skipping the most recent month. Long the winners, short the losers.
momentum.literature: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993); Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013) "Value and Momentum Everywhere"

value.label: Value (book-to-price)
value.blurb: Book-to-price with the most recent book value and the current price rather than the price at the fiscal year end. Long cheap, short expensive.

value_composite.label: Value (composite)
value_composite.blurb: Multi-measure value: standardised log book-to-price, log sales-to-price, cash-flow-to-price and earnings-to-price averaged, all on current prices.
value_composite.literature: Asness, Frazzini, Israel & Moskowitz (2015) "Fact, Fiction and Value Investing"

quality.label: Quality (profitability, growth, safety)
quality.blurb: Three pillars: profitability (gross profits, ROE, ROA, cash flow over assets, gross margin, low accruals), growth (their five-year change) and safety (low beta, low leverage, low O-score, high Z-score, stable earnings), each a z-score of ranks, summed and standardised.
quality.literature: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2019), Review of Accounting Studies

low_beta.label: Low beta (beta-neutral)
low_beta.blurb: Names ranked by a shrunk beta (one-year volatility ratio times the five-year correlation of three-day returns, 0.6 beta + 0.4); low-beta names long, levered to beta one, high-beta names short, de-levered to beta one.
low_beta.literature: Black, Jensen & Scholes (1972); Frazzini & Pedersen (2014), Journal of Financial Economics

size.label: Size
size.blurb: Small minus big: long the small half of the universe by market value, short the big half, value-weighted. Within the liquid, point-in-time universe the ADV floor leaves.
size.literature: Fama & French (1993) SMB; Asness, Frazzini, Israel, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2018) "Size Matters, If You Control Your Junk"

investment.label: Investment
investment.blurb: Conservative minus aggressive: minus one-year growth in total assets. Firms that grow their balance sheet fastest earn less.

reversal.label: Short-term reversal
reversal.blurb: Minus the past month's return. Liquidity provision: last month's losers bounce. The fastest factor and the most cost-sensitive.

mom_12_7.label: Intermediate momentum (12-7)
mom_12_7.blurb: The cumulative return over months t-12 to t-7 only. The older half of the momentum window, which carries most of the effect in the original study.

resid_mom.label: Residual momentum
resid_mom.blurb: Momentum in the part of the return the market does not explain: the 12-1 sum of market-model residuals (three-year fit) over their standard deviation. Half the volatility of plain momentum and far smaller crashes.
resid_mom.literature: Blitz, Huij & Martens (2011), Journal of Empirical Finance

ind_mom.label: Industry momentum
ind_mom.blurb: Each name scored by the six-month cap-weighted return of its industry. Long the names in winning industries, short those in losing ones.

high_52w.label: 52-week high
high_52w.blurb: The price over its highest level of the past year. Names near the high keep rising: investors anchor on it and under-react to good news.

seasonality.label: Return seasonality
seasonality.blurb: The average return of the coming calendar month in each of the last five years. A name that did well in past Decembers tends to do well this December.
seasonality.literature: Heston & Sadka (2008), Journal of Financial Economics

rev_ind.label: Industry-adjusted reversal
rev_ind.blurb: Minus the past month's return in excess of the name's industry. Taking out the industry move leaves the liquidity-driven part of reversal and drops the industry momentum that works against it.

lt_reversal.label: Long-term reversal (60-13)
lt_reversal.blurb: Minus the return over months t-60 to t-13. Five-year losers outperform five-year winners.
lt_reversal.literature: De Bondt & Thaler (1985), Journal of Finance

earnings_yield.label: Earnings yield
earnings_yield.blurb: Trailing twelve-month net income to common shareholders over the current market value.

fcf_yield.label: Free-cash-flow yield
fcf_yield.blurb: Trailing twelve-month operating cash flow less capital expenditure, over the current market value.
fcf_yield.literature: Lakonishok, Shleifer & Vishny (1994), Journal of Finance

ebitda_ev.label: EBITDA to enterprise value
ebitda_ev.blurb: Trailing EBITDA over enterprise value (market value plus debt less cash). Capital-structure neutral, so a levered firm is not cheap by construction. Financials are left out.
ebitda_ev.literature: Loughran & Wellman (2011), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis

shareholder_yield.label: Shareholder yield
shareholder_yield.blurb: Dividend yield plus net buyback yield (minus the one-year growth in the share count). What the firm hands back, whichever way it does it.
shareholder_yield.literature: Boudoukh, Michaely, Richardson & Roberts (2007), Journal of Finance

dividend_yield.label: Dividend yield (payers)
dividend_yield.blurb: Trailing twelve-month dividends over price, ranked among the names that pay one.

value_intangible.label: Intangibles-adjusted book-to-price
value_intangible.blurb: Book value plus capitalised intangibles (R&D amortised at 15% a year, 30% of SG&A at 20%) less goodwill, over market value. Book-to-price for firms whose assets are not on the balance sheet.

gross_profit.label: Gross profitability
gross_profit.blurb: Trailing gross profit over total assets.

op_profit.label: Operating profitability
op_profit.blurb: Revenue less cost of goods, SG&A and interest, over book equity.
op_profit.literature: Fama & French (2015), Journal of Financial Economics

cash_profit.label: Cash-based operating profitability
cash_profit.blurb: Operating profit with the accruals taken out (changes in receivables, inventory, payables and deferred revenue), over total assets.
cash_profit.literature: Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa & Nikolaev (2016), Journal of Financial Economics

roe.label: Return on equity
roe.blurb: Trailing net income over book equity.

roic.label: Return on invested capital
roic.blurb: Trailing EBIT over invested capital (debt plus equity less cash). Financials are left out.

quality_classic.label: Quality (ROE, low debt, stable earnings)
quality_classic.blurb: The index providers' quality: high return on equity, low debt to equity and low five-year earnings variability, the three z-scores averaged.
quality_classic.literature: the published index-provider quality methodologies (ROE, debt to equity, earnings variability)

fscore.label: Piotroski F-score
fscore.blurb: Nine yes-or-no tests of improving fundamentals: positive income and cash flow, cash flow above income, rising return on assets, margin and asset turnover, falling leverage, rising liquidity, no new shares.

accruals.label: Accruals
accruals.blurb: Minus the non-cash part of earnings (the change in working capital less depreciation) over total assets. Earnings made of accruals reverse.

pct_accruals.label: Percent accruals
pct_accruals.blurb: Minus accruals (net income less operating cash flow) over the absolute level of net income instead of assets.
pct_accruals.literature: Hafzalla, Lundholm & Van Winkle (2011), The Accounting Review

noa.label: Net operating assets
noa.blurb: Minus operating assets less operating liabilities, over lagged total assets. A balance sheet bloated by years of accruals.
noa.literature: Hirshleifer, Hou, Teoh & Zhang (2004), Journal of Accounting and Economics

earn_stability.label: Earnings stability
earn_stability.blurb: Minus the five-year volatility of return on equity.
earn_stability.literature: Dichev & Tang (2009), Journal of Accounting and Economics

low_leverage.label: Low leverage
low_leverage.blurb: Minus total debt over total assets.
low_leverage.literature: Penman, Richardson & Tuna (2007), Journal of Accounting Research

distress.label: Low distress (O-score, Z-score)
distress.blurb: Low bankruptcy probability on two accounting models: the Ohlson O-score (low is safe) and the Altman Z-score (high is safe), the two z-scores averaged.
distress.literature: Ohlson (1980); Altman (1968); Dichev (1998); Campbell, Hilscher & Szilagyi (2008)

margin_trend.label: Margin and turnover trend
margin_trend.blurb: The one-year change in gross margin and in asset turnover, the two z-scores averaged. The two legs of an improving return on assets.
margin_trend.literature: Soliman (2008), The Accounting Review; Abarbanell & Bushee (1998)

beneish.label: Beneish M-score
beneish.blurb: Minus the earnings-manipulation score: ratios on receivables, margin, asset quality, sales growth, depreciation, SG&A, leverage and accruals that separated restating firms from the rest. Financials are left out.
beneish.literature: Beneish (1999), Financial Analysts Journal; Beneish, Lee & Nichols (2013)

rd_intensity.label: R&D intensity
rd_intensity.blurb: Trailing research and development expense over market value, among the names that report one. A measurement as much as a factor: many names report no R&D.
rd_intensity.literature: Chan, Lakonishok & Sougiannis (2001), Journal of Finance

cash_conversion.label: Cash conversion
cash_conversion.blurb: Operating cash flow over net income for profitable firms. A measurement of how much of reported profit arrives as cash.

net_issuance.label: Net share issuance
net_issuance.blurb: Minus the one-year log growth in the split-adjusted share count. Buyers of their own shares outperform issuers.
net_issuance.literature: Pontiff & Woodgate (2008), Journal of Finance; Fama & French (2008)

composite_issuance.label: Composite equity issuance
composite_issuance.blurb: Minus the five-year growth in market value that did not come from the stock's return: issues, buybacks and dividends together.

ext_financing.label: Net external financing
ext_financing.blurb: Minus net equity issued plus net debt raised less dividends, over average total assets. Financials are left out.
ext_financing.literature: Bradshaw, Richardson & Sloan (2006), Journal of Accounting and Economics

capex_inventory.label: Investment to assets
capex_inventory.blurb: Minus the one-year change in gross plant and inventory over lagged total assets.
capex_inventory.literature: Lyandres, Sun & Zhang (2008), Review of Financial Studies; Chen, Novy-Marx & Zhang (2011)

low_vol.label: Low volatility
low_vol.blurb: Minus one-year realised volatility, dollar neutral. A plain long-short of calm against wild names: it carries a short market beta, which the beta-neutral version removes.
low_vol.literature: Haugen & Heins (1975); Blitz & van Vliet (2007), Journal of Portfolio Management

low_vol_bn.label: Low volatility (beta-neutral)
low_vol_bn.blurb: Names ranked by one-year volatility; the calm leg levered and the wild leg de-levered until each has a beta of one, so the book has no market exposure.
low_vol_bn.literature: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014); Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011), Financial Analysts Journal

ivol.label: Idiosyncratic volatility
ivol.blurb: Minus the volatility of the past month's market-model residuals.
ivol.literature: Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang (2006), Journal of Finance

lottery.label: Lottery demand (MAX)
lottery.blurb: Minus the average of the five highest daily returns of the past month. Names that just had lottery-like jumps are overpaid for.
lottery.literature: Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw (2011), Journal of Financial Economics

iskew.label: Idiosyncratic skewness
iskew.blurb: Minus the one-year skewness of market-model residuals. Positive skew is a lottery ticket and is priced like one.
iskew.literature: Boyer, Mitton & Vorkink (2010), Review of Financial Studies; Harvey & Siddique (2000)

downside_beta.label: Downside beta
downside_beta.blurb: Beta measured only on days the market is below its one-year average. A risk premium, not an anomaly: names that fall hardest in falling markets should earn more. Kept out of the low-risk composite for that reason.
downside_beta.literature: Ang, Chen & Xing (2006), Review of Financial Studies

illiquidity.label: Illiquidity (Amihud)
illiquidity.blurb: The one-year average of the absolute daily return per million dollars traded. Names that are costly to trade earn a premium, inside a universe that already has an ADV floor.

turnover.label: Low share turnover
turnover.blurb: Minus the one-year average of traded value over market value. Heavily traded names underperform quiet ones.
turnover.literature: Datar, Naik & Radcliffe (1998), Journal of Financial Markets

volume_shock.label: Volume shock
volume_shock.blurb: The past week's traded value against the ten weeks before it, in standard deviations. A burst of volume brings attention and a few weeks of higher returns.
volume_shock.literature: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin (2001), Journal of Finance

sue.label: Earnings surprise (SUE)
sue.blurb: The latest interim net income less the same period a year earlier, over the standard deviation of the previous eight such changes. Known on the filing date. Prices drift in the direction of the surprise for months.

rev_surprise.label: Revenue surprise
rev_surprise.blurb: The same seasonal surprise on revenue. Sales are harder to manage than earnings and the drift after them is separate.
rev_surprise.literature: Jegadeesh & Livnat (2006), Journal of Accounting and Economics

ann_return.label: Announcement return
ann_return.blurb: The name's return less the market's over the four sessions around its last earnings report, entered the session after the window closes. The market's own verdict on the report, with no forecast needed.
ann_return.literature: Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok (1996), Journal of Finance; Brandt, Kishore, Santa-Clara & Venkatachalam (2008)

eps_surprise.label: Consensus EPS surprise
eps_surprise.blurb: Reported earnings per share less the analyst consensus, over the price a week before the report.
eps_surprise.literature: Livnat & Mendenhall (2006), Journal of Accounting Research

ann_premium.label: Announcement premium
ann_premium.blurb: Long the names about to report, short those that just have. Expected report dates are a year after past ones, so nothing here needs the company's own calendar.
ann_premium.literature: Frazzini & Lamont (2007); Barber, De George, Lehavy & Trueman (2013), Journal of Financial Economics

comp_momentum.label: Momentum composite
comp_momentum.blurb: The four trend measures averaged: 12-1 momentum, residual momentum, industry momentum and the 52-week high. The reversals and seasonality are separate effects and stay out.
comp_momentum.literature: the members of the family, equal weight

comp_value.label: Value composite (broad)
comp_value.blurb: Six measures averaged: book-to-price, intangibles-adjusted book-to-price, earnings yield, free-cash-flow yield, EBITDA to enterprise value and shareholder yield.
comp_value.literature: the members of the family, equal weight

comp_quality.label: Quality composite (broad)
comp_quality.blurb: Four themes at equal weight: profitability (gross, operating, cash-based, ROE, ROIC), earnings quality (low accruals, percent accruals, net operating assets, M-score), safety (low leverage, stable earnings, O-score, Z-score) and improvement (F-score, margin and turnover trend).
comp_quality.literature: the members of the family, four themes at equal weight

comp_investment.label: Investment composite
comp_investment.blurb: Five measures of a firm growing or raising capital, averaged and shorted: asset growth, net share issuance, composite issuance, net external financing, investment to assets.
comp_investment.literature: the members of the family, equal weight

comp_low_risk.label: Low-risk composite
comp_low_risk.blurb: Low volatility, low beta, low idiosyncratic volatility, low MAX and low skewness averaged. Dollar neutral, so it carries a short market beta.
comp_low_risk.literature: the members of the family, equal weight

comp_liquidity.label: Illiquidity composite
comp_liquidity.blurb: Small, illiquid and quietly traded: minus log market value, log Amihud illiquidity and minus share turnover, averaged.
comp_liquidity.literature: the members of the family, equal weight

comp_earnings.label: Earnings composite
comp_earnings.blurb: The earnings and revenue surprises, the announcement return and the consensus surprise averaged; the last two only where the market's earnings calendar covers the universe.
comp_earnings.literature: the members of the family, equal weight

magic_formula.label: Magic formula
magic_formula.blurb: Good companies at cheap prices: return on capital (EBIT over net working capital plus net fixed assets) and earnings yield (EBIT over enterprise value), averaged. Z-scores where the original sums ranks. Financials are left out.
magic_formula.literature: Greenblatt (2006), The Little Book That Beats the Market

short_interest.label: Short interest
short_interest.blurb: Minus shares sold short over shares outstanding. Short sellers are informed: heavily shorted names underperform. US from FINRA (twice monthly, from 2018), Australia from ASIC (daily, from 2010), Hong Kong from the SFC (weekly, from 2012), the UK from the FCA (disclosed positions of 0.5% or more to July 2026, the aggregate after).
short_interest.literature: Asquith, Pathak & Ritter (2005); Boehmer, Huszar & Jordan (2010); Rapach, Ringgenberg & Zhou (2016)

days_to_cover.label: Days to cover
days_to_cover.blurb: Minus short interest over average daily volume: how many days of normal trading the shorts would need to close. Shorting is cheaper to hold in liquid names, so scaling by volume separates conviction from convenience.
days_to_cover.literature: Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman & Yan (2016), "Days to Cover and Stock Returns"

si_change.label: Change in short interest
si_change.blurb: Minus the change in short interest over the past month, as a share of shares outstanding. New shorting carries the information; old positions are stale.
si_change.literature: Desai, Ramesh, Thiagarajan & Balachandran (2002); Boehmer, Jones & Zhang (2008)

short_volume.label: Short-sale volume
short_volume.blurb: Minus the share of the past month's off-exchange volume that was sold short (FINRA daily files, from 2009). The flow behind short interest, seen daily.
short_volume.literature: Boehmer, Jones & Zhang (2008), Journal of Finance; Diether, Lee & Werner (2009)

fails.label: Fails to deliver
fails.blurb: Minus the average daily shares failed to deliver over shares outstanding (SEC, half-monthly). Persistent fails mark names that are hard to borrow.

insider_buying.label: Insider net buying
insider_buying.blurb: Open-market purchases less sales by officers and directors over the past six months (SEC Form 4, on the filing date). Insiders sell for many reasons and buy for one.
insider_buying.literature: Lakonishok & Lee (2001), Review of Financial Studies; Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (2012)

comp_positioning.label: Positioning composite
comp_positioning.blurb: Short interest, days to cover and the change in short interest, averaged and shorted; in the US also short-sale volume, fails to deliver, and insider net buying (long).
comp_positioning.literature: the members of the family, equal weight
